verdict.rationale: cubic runs unattended on GitHub pull requests. It reviews every new PR automatically and can auto-fix and auto-approve without a human in the loop. It also ships a CLI that reviews local changes and emits a fix prompt for coding agents. However, the evidence never documents running the CLI headlessly in a CI pipeline (e.g. a GitHub Actions step, non-interactive flags, exit codes or machine-readable output). Missing for 10: documented CI/headless mode for the CLI, non-interactive auth/exit-code/output-format docs, CI integration examples, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Once installed, cubic automatically reviews new pull requests.
turn on auto-fix to have cubic fix the issues from every review of a pull request.
Auto-approval lets you skip human review for pull requests that cubic determines are low risk and issue-free.
The cubic CLI reviews local changes before you push. It finds bugs and generates a prompt that your coding agent can use to fix them.
